question: The furnished products.aspose.org page for pdf/net states the library 'exposes 805 classes'. Our own extraction (TC-011, upstream commit b717287) found 899 TYPES. In the 300-type reduced fixture the kind split is 215 class_declaration / 81 enum / 3 interface / 1 struct, so 805 classes out of 899 types is not obviously reconcilable - extrapolating the sample gives roughly 644 classes, and the mission plan's own independent figure is 863. Three sources, three numbers, none currently cross-checked.
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: ingest the page, but the 805-classes sentence is marked unverified and must not be served as a citable fact until it is cross-checked against a full (non-reduced) extraction.
rationale: This is exactly the defect class the mission plan exists to prevent - a furnished page asserting a precise number that the deterministic tier does not corroborate. It cannot be resolved now because TC-011 deliberately committed a 300-type REDUCED fixture, so we cannot count classes across the full surface. TC-014 is the card that builds citation verification against raw knowledge; it is the right place to settle this. Blocking work now would stall the queue over a question that a later card is designed to answer.

question: search_docs doc content is sourced from repository-presenter's local sealed candidates rather than a live upstream README fetch, because repository-presenter cannot yet push to upstream repos and there is no tag or Co-Authored-By trailer to verify a live README's provenance. When should this switch to a live upstream fetch?
provisional_decision: Read repository-presenter's own local sealed candidate store (candidates/<org>__<repo>/CURRENT -> README.md) for now. Switch TC-119's source back to a live raw.githubusercontent.com fetch (this card's original, superseded design) once BOTH: (1) repository-presenter can push README changes to the real upstream repos, and (2) the resulting live commit/README carries an identifying tag or a Co-Authored-By: Repository Presenter <...>-style trailer marking its origin, so the switch itself is verifiable rather than assumed.
rationale: repository-presenter's own README documents real grounding/validation discipline (facts from the repo's own source/tests/examples, independent non-authoring review, proven reproducibility) that materially exceeds aspose.org's unreviewed pages - but its own project status confirms it does not yet open PRs against target repos, so a live upstream README's provenance cannot yet be machine-verified. The local sealed candidate is the strongest currently-verifiable source.

question: pdf/typescript has no sealed repository-presenter candidate yet (confirmed 2026-09-28: only an unsealed runs/clones/ checkout and a runs/transactions/<rev>/source/ snapshot exist under repository-presenter, no candidates/aspose-pdf-foss__Aspose.PDF-FOSS-for-TypeScript/CURRENT). TC-119 therefore excludes it and leaves its furnished fixture on the old aspose.org-copied content. When should pdf/typescript's doc content be regenerated?
provisional_decision: Leave pdf/typescript's tests/fixtures/furnished/pdf_typescript/pages/_index.md unchanged by TC-119. Regenerate it the same way as the other 5 pilots (via a small follow-up card reusing TC-119's sealed_candidate_doc_fields) as soon as candidates/aspose-pdf-foss__Aspose.PDF-FOSS-for-TypeScript/CURRENT exists in repository-presenter's own store.
rationale: Do not work around the gap by fetching pdf/typescript's live upstream README instead - that would reintroduce the unverifiable-provenance problem OQ-002 exists to avoid for the other 5 pilots, and do not fabricate sealed-candidate-shaped content that does not exist. An honest, tracked gap for one pilot is preferable to a silently inconsistent pipeline.

question: foss_mcp.normalization.document_schema.to_dict/from_dict (NormalizedDocument <-> JSON-able dict round-trip, schema_version-tagged) have zero production callers - infra/build_chunks.py builds a NormalizedDocument and immediately chunks it in-memory, never persisting/reloading it independently. The shape (explicit schema_version, nested Provenance/ValidationResult reconstruction) strongly suggests an intentional future document-level persistence/cache layer rather than leftover cruft, but no current card specifies one. Wire (build that persistence layer), or delete as premature API?
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: leave to_dict/from_dict in place, unwired, exactly as-is. Do not delete (deleting a deliberately-shaped, round-trip-tested serialization API on code-level suspicion alone risks destroying a real future requirement for no measured benefit) and do not speculatively build a persistence layer with no consumer or requirement naming it (would violate this project's own no-speculative-abstraction discipline). Revisit when either (a) a future card needs document-level caching/persistence and can name a real consumer, or (b) a future unwired-symbol audit round has no remaining evidence of planned use, at which point delete.
rationale: Unlike with_validation (citation.py's validate_chunk already duplicates its exact logic inline - clear evidence of supersession, resolved by wiring without this open question) or build_manifest (a live production duplicate-construction site exists to wire into), to_dict/from_dict have no adjacent code either consuming them or duplicating their logic - there is no code-level signal pointing to wire vs delete, only a plausible but unconfirmed guess about future intent. Per AGENTS.md, a question the loop cannot answer from the evidence becomes a recorded provisional decision, not a stall.

question: The product-reference fetch (infra/fetch_product_reference.py via src/foss_mcp/extraction/manifest_reader.fetch_manifest_file) calls the unauthenticated GitHub Contents API, 60 requests per hour per IP. In the 2026-10-05 fourteen-pilot live run, cells-rust, slides-java and cells-go ingestion Jobs failed three times each with HTTP 403 rate limit exceeded, and because the fetch runs after publish and a failed Job blocks the serving init container, their serving pods never started. Should the fetch accept a token and should a rate-limited fetch stop blocking serving?
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: leave the fetch unauthenticated for the POC and retry the rate-limited pilots after the hourly reset (verified: quota 30 of 60 remaining at 00:32, reset 01:21). Before any real deployment, add an optional GITHUB_TOKEN header read from a Kubernetes secret the owner provisions, and make a 403 or 429 retry with backoff and Retry-After instead of failing the Job. A credential is an owner item.
rationale: The failure is an environment quota, not a code defect, so it must not be hidden by weakening a check. It is still a real production fragility: a transient 403 permanently blocks a pilot unless the Job is rerun by hand. The token itself is an owner-only credential, so it cannot be done by the loop.

question: The cells/cpp and pdf/cpp pilots serve symbols but no documentation, because infra/build_chunks.py has no cpp entry in _PLATFORM_DISPATCH, so a furnished page cannot be ingested for C++ without a C++ example verifier. The verifier in src/foss_mcp/indexing/example_verifier.py is MSVC-only and cells-specific. When is the Linux g++/CMake verify path built so C++ documentation and verified examples are ingested?
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: the POC proves C++ on the checks that apply (symbols, lookup, members, product reference, freshness, honest miss, isolation) and records search_docs and verified examples as not applicable for the two C++ pilots. Build a prepare/verify pair for cpp that compiles in the Linux container (feasible: pdf/cpp built with g++ 14 and CMake 3.31, recorded 2026-10-04), add the cpp entry to _PLATFORM_DISPATCH, then wire furnishedPage for cells/cpp and pdf/cpp.
rationale: Presenting a C++ pilot as documentation-complete without a verifier would claim verified examples that were never compiled. The gap is real, large, and independent of the MCP serving path, so it is tracked and not hidden.

question: The Linux C++ verifier (prepare_cpp_library_linux / verify_cpp_example_linux, TC-222) has never executed. Its one live test is deselected here, and this Windows host has no Linux g++ on PATH. Has the real pinned pdf/cpp library built and a real example verified inside the Linux ingestion image?
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: the offline tests with subprocess mocked, the dispatch wiring and the negative control prove the code paths; the live proof is a G3 requirement. Run the live test in the Linux ingestion image (FOSS_MCP_NETWORK_TESTS=1, the image built by scripts/release/build_images.py) and record its result before G3 exit.

question: The Linux C++ build needs network at build time: cmake configure downloads googletest from github.com (FetchContent) and the pinned library is fetched with git. Apt packages g++ and cmake are not pinned by exact version in Dockerfile.ingestion, and toolchain.lock.json has no row for them. Is this acceptable residual risk?
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: keep the floating apt pins, following the file's existing rule for openjdk and maven, and record the exact versions in the Dockerfile comment (g++ 4:14.2.0-1, cmake 3.31.6-2). Add lock rows and an offline build path (a vendored googletest or a build-time network allowance) under a governed card before any production deployment.
rationale: The configure step cannot run without GitHub, the same origin as the pinned fetch the pipeline already needs. Exact apt pins would break on the next trixie update. Both are residual risks, recorded here rather than hidden.

question: ops/gatecli.py _source_ref_problems() hard-fails validate for ~300 already-accepted cards whose source_ref cites the retired external mission-plan file (C:\Users\prora\.claude\plans\mission-plan-and-stateful-sprout.md), per the explicit 2026-10-10 operator decision to stop depending on it. That alone was already an accepted condition, but scripts/ci_check.sh hard-fails its gatectl step on any validate problem, which made .githooks/pre-push refuse every push unconditionally - discovered while pushing the git-identity incident fix. Is grandfathering source_refs entirely once a card holds an accepted receipt (mirroring the existing cardlint accepted-grandfather precedent) the right permanent fix, or should source_refs instead be re-pointed at internal taskcards/DECISION_LOG entries per card?
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: _source_ref_problems() now skips both the file-existence and hash-drift checks entirely once a card holds an accepted receipt - source_refs justified a card at AUTHORING time; once accepted, that justification is historical record, not a live constraint. An unaccepted card whose cited file truly vanishes is still a real authoring problem and is NOT grandfathered. This unblocks every push immediately; re-pointing ~300 cards individual source_refs at internal taskcards is unnecessary busywork for cards already done.
rationale: A full push outage (not merely a validate-output nuisance) is a severe, previously-unrecognized consequence of a condition already declared accepted. Fixing it narrowly (grandfather on acceptance, same precedent already used for cardlint and this file text itself) unblocks work now without reopening the original decision or hand-editing state.yaml or any receipt.

question: OQ-002 resolved that furnished documentation pages are generated only from repository-presenter's local sealed candidate READMEs, never from a live upstream fetch. Only five pilots have a sealed candidate, so 34 pilots have no documentation page and no verified examples. May pages for the other pilots be generated once from the library README at the pinned commit through the authenticated GitHub reader and committed as fixtures?
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: yes. The README is pinned to the same library commit as the extracted symbols, the generated page is committed as a fixture so every rebuild stays offline and deterministic, the generator refuses a README too thin to be documentation and omits sections it lacks rather than inventing them, and a generic fixture-validity test pins every page. The sealed path for the original five pilots is unchanged.
rationale: OQ-002's intent was network independence and reviewed content. Both hold for a committed, commit-pinned fixture. Without this, at most six pilots can ever have documentation, which cannot meet the operator's bar of at least 10 to 20 complete pilots for peer testing.

question: Should the standalone image bake offline (hashing-provider) query vectors so find_examples can use vector search without the embedding gateway?
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: no. Ship gateway vectors for example chunks plus lexical matching; state the example-search mode visibly (report_index_freshness example_search field, startup log, /readyz header) and list it as a known limitation in docs/RELEASE.md.
rationale: Measured on 14 committed examples with HashingEmbeddingProvider at 64/256/1024 dims: true-query scores 0.159-0.599 while nonsense queries reach 0.507 (64d) and 0.267 (1024d), so no threshold separates them; every true query already has lexical coverage 1.0; a bag-of-words hash adds only partial-overlap matches the TC-273 coverage floor rejects on purpose (the TC-399 nonsense defect). A real offline semantic model is not feasible in the lean image by Monday.

question: tex/python: the upstream library at the pinned commit (also HEAD) does not import (35 of 45 files have collapsed indentation). Keep the pilot in the image, drop it, or keep it with a warning?
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: keep the pilot (the repaired API reference is correct and useful) and make get_product_reference(install), report_index_freshness and the extraction notice state plainly that the library cannot be imported at this commit, with the true count of unparseable files.
rationale: R9 ran the workflow and could not import the package, R5 verified the repaired signatures against the source text with 0 mismatches in 23 live checks, and the operator's rule is complete, not partial, for every pilot included: dropping would be a scope decision for the operator, a warning keeps the data honest. Resolved: TC-561 (ACCEPTED) made get_product_reference install text, report_index_freshness and the extraction notice state plainly that tex/python cannot be imported at the pinned commit, with the true unparseable-file count.

question: Drift: the indexed source commit is ahead of the published package for slides/python, 3d/java, 3d/net and slides/java (3d/net documents 103 types the NuGet package lacks). Index the published version instead of the pinned commit, or disclose?
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: keep indexing the pinned commit, and detect and disclose drift per pilot (index_ahead_of_package with the commit distance and the published version in report_index_freshness and in the install notice, with the build-from-commit instruction spelled out).
rationale: The commit is the only version for which docs, examples and symbols are consistent; the published packages are older snapshots of the same repositories and eleven pilots have no package at all. Disclosure removes the silent failure the review demonstrated; reindexing per registry version is a different product. Resolved: TC-560 (ACCEPTED) added index_ahead_of_package drift detection and disclosure (commit distance + published version) in report_index_freshness and the install notice for slides/python, 3d/java, 3d/net and slides/java.

question: Symbols whose body is NotImplementedError or whose documentation says unsupported (3d/python 734 members, 3d/net Render, SaveFormat members that cannot be saved): remove them from the index or mark them?
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: mark, do not remove. A served member carries an explicit 'unsupported or not implemented in this build' marker derived from the source body or the scope documentation, and lookup surfaces the limitation when the query names the capability.
rationale: An agent that does not find a symbol will look elsewhere or invent it, while a marked symbol tells it exactly why the call fails; removing would also hide the surface the README describes. Resolved: TC-559 (ACCEPTED) added explicit stub/unsupported-or-not-implemented markers derived from the source body or scope documentation, and lookup surfaces the limitation when a query names the capability.

question: OWNER-14 records that the GitHub token in the cluster Secret is rejected (HTTP 401). The closing re-ingest of all 32 pilots refetches product references and releases from GitHub. Wait for the operator to replace the token, or proceed?
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: proceed. First probe the token with a status-code-only request (never print it). If it is valid, re-ingest normally. If it is not, re-ingest with the previous snapshot's sidecars carried forward for every pilot whose fetch fails (the snapshot tool's allow-missing-sidecars route used for pdf/cpp), keep their fetched_at stamps, and record the carry-forward per pilot in the closing evidence; never publish a fetch_failed sidecar over a good one.
rationale: The review's own sidecar and release checks (R4, R12) show the baked sidecars are accurate to GitHub today; a degraded refetch would be a regression, and the token is an owner-only credential that must not block the data fixes. The operator can replace the token at any time and a later refresh is a data-only change. Resolved: TC-536 (ACCEPTED, the closing re-ingest) probed the token, found it still rejected, and carried forward the previous snapshot sidecars for the affected pilots (pdf/cpp via --allow-missing-sidecars) rather than publishing a fetch_failed sidecar over a good one; recorded in the TC-536/ad8c2329 evidence.

provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: accept the measured rate and pin WRONG_MAX at 4.5 percent as a ratchet that may only go down; allow one targeted pdf improvement inside the card. Re-measure on the final data in the independent QA round and file a card if the QA corpus shows more than 5 percent.
question: TC-562 asked for a confidently-wrong (non-empty, not labelled partial, intended API absent from the first 10 results) rate of at most 2 percent on the 729-case retrieval corpus. The worker measured 3.6 percent overall (baseline 17.3 percent) and 9.9 percent for the pdf family. Accept, or keep tuning?
rationale: Hit-rate at 3 rose from 0.53 to 0.86 and the confidently-wrong rate fell fivefold; the remaining misses are lexical-retrieval limits (no embeddings) and further tuning on the same corpus risks overfitting. The 2 percent figure was an estimate written before the baseline was measured. Re-measured 2026-10-23 against the final re-ingested data (commit 46e9e097, post TC-536/TC-571/TC-572): confidently-wrong fell to 3.29 percent overall (was 3.6) but pdf is 8.55 percent (was 9.9) - this is ABOVE the 5 percent card-file bar this decision itself set, not below it (a 2026-10-23 resolution of this entry incorrectly asserted both numbers were under 5 percent; that was a plain arithmetic error, caught and reverted the same day, never acted on beyond the one-line JSONL edit). Per the decision's own stated bar, a card is warranted. Also found in the same audit: the aggregate WRONG_MAX=4.5 percent ratchet test has no per-family equivalent, so a family-specific regression this size can clear the aggregate test indefinitely without ever being caught again. Resolved: TC-579 (ACCEPTED) added a WRONG_MAX_FAMILY per-family ratchet (tests/mcp/tools/test_round3_retrieval_corpus.py) pinned to each family's own measured rate plus a small margin, closing the exact blind spot this entry named. A supervisor-commissioned investigation of pdf's retrieval code found no single missing synonym or lever - pdf's six platform libraries name the same real-world task under structurally different API vocabulary, so the miss is diffuse across many query/API pairs, not one fixable bug. Rather than chase further tuning (risking overfitting this fixed corpus, the exact risk this entry already flagged), TC-579 published pdf's higher rate as an honestly-disclosed, causally-explained known limitation (docs/RELEASE.md L-142).

provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: accept the measured largest-file size and the worker's pinned LARGEST_FILE_BYTES_BUDGET=6,060,000 (measured x1.05, rounded up). The 4.5M figure in the card's prose was already stale before this dispatch: TC-553 pinned LARGEST_FILE_BYTES_BUDGET to 5,360,000 (above 4.5M) pre-Round-3 with no stop raised then either, so it was never a live-enforced test assertion, only narrative guidance written when the review's TC-527 estimate (about 3.3M) was current. The one ceiling that IS mechanically enforced in the suite, LEAN_CEILING_BYTES=45,000,000 bytes for the whole tree, is satisfied (41,732,902). scripts/release/generation_diff.py confirms the html/python growth (nearly every signature line rewritten, members 26,996->27,098) traces to legitimate per-member documentation and marker text from the accepted Round-3 cards (TC-557 throws/varargs/implicit-constructor lines, TC-559 stub markers, TC-560 drift sentences, TC-561 install-truth text), not a runaway or defective extraction.
question: TC-536's own card text says to STOP (FAILED_INTERNAL) if the re-ingested tree's largest generation file exceeds 4,500,000 bytes. The supervisor's pre-dispatch amendment wrongly claimed all four size-regression numbers were under their ceilings; the measured largest (html/python, 5,771,402 bytes) actually breaches the 4.5M prose ceiling, though the tree total (41,732,902) is well under the only mechanically-enforced ceiling, LEAN_CEILING_BYTES=45,000,000 (TC-553). Stop and roll back the re-ingest, or accept the measured size and pin LARGEST_FILE_BYTES_BUDGET to it plus headroom?
rationale: A stale prose ceiling written against an estimate that Round-3's own fidelity fixes (which this gate exists to ship) were always going to exceed is not a reason to roll back 32 pilots of correctly re-ingested, independently-reviewed data; the real safety rail (LEAN_CEILING_BYTES, enforced by a live test) holds. If a future re-ingest approaches 45,000,000 the live test fails and forces a real decision then. Resolved: TC-536 (ACCEPTED) shipped with LARGEST_FILE_BYTES_BUDGET pinned to the measured largest file (6,060,000, x1.05 headroom); the one mechanically-enforced ceiling, LEAN_CEILING_BYTES=45,000,000 for the whole tree, is satisfied (41,732,902). The 4.5M figure in the card prose was already stale pre-Round-3 (TC-553 pinned 5,360,000 with no stop raised then either).

question: TC-590's real live run of the new Rust oracle against the real pinned cells/rust commit (aspose-cells-foss/Aspose.Cells-FOSS-for-Rust @ 1a6004af47b1ef15385f9d36d381a8172428cc7e) found a non-empty diff against tests/fixtures/cells_rust/api_surface.json: 341 missing (syntactically-pub internal ...Model structs that sit behind the crate's real public-facing wrapper types, e.g. AutoFilterColorFilterModel behind AutoFilterColorFilter) and 14 signature findings (CellObjectValue's several literally-named-from impl From<T> methods all compared against one fixture entry by bare name). Both are real extraction-fidelity questions the oracle surfaced, not an oracle defect (TC-590's worker traced both root causes directly); telling a crate's real public API apart from its pub-but-unreachable internals needs a module-reachability resolver, outside this card's literal pub-struct/enum/trait scope.
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: record as a known, honestly-disclosed extraction-fidelity gap for cells/rust (341 missing, 14 signature). Not fixed by this card (out of its literal scope) and not blocking G3 - a future card can add module-reachability filtering to enumerate_rust (or to the tree-sitter rust extractor, whichever is the right layer) if this pilot is ever re-prioritized for fidelity work.
rationale: The whole point of TC-566/TC-589/TC-590 is an INDEPENDENT oracle that is honest about what it finds, including findings about this project's own extraction fixture, not only about the oracle's own correctness. Blocking the gate on this would conflate 'the oracle works' with 'the pilot's api_surface.json fixture is already perfectly faithful', which was never this card's claim - its claim is a working, proven independent diff tool, delivered.

question: TC-591's real live run of the new TypeScript oracle against the real pinned pdf/typescript commit (aspose-pdf-foss/Aspose.PDF-FOSS-for-TypeScript @ 155bfc7a33f0ba23fb4252b6ba201828b02a5b9d) found a non-empty diff against tests/fixtures/pdf_typescript/api_surface.json: checked=2498, missing=258, extra=29, signature=1 (all other categories 0). The worker traced each: (1) signature(1) is a pure serialization-convention mismatch for Document.Merge's rest parameter ('...docs' in the fixture's raw text vs the Compiler API's bare identifier 'docs'), not a content error. (2) missing(258), the dominant finding: this library pervasively uses TypeScript's constructor-parameter-property shorthand (e.g. `constructor(protected readonly doc: Document, readonly Dict: PdfDict) {}`), and the baked fixture never lists ANY of these as members - not even the fully public, no-modifier ones - verified directly against src/annotation.ts and src/formfield.ts. This is either a real parameter-property blind spot in the tree-sitter TypeScript extractor, or a deliberate exclusion of constructor-set fields from the documented surface; it recurs across dozens of classes, so it is a real, structural fidelity question for this pilot, not noise. (3) extra(29): the fixture lists explicit 'constructor' method entries this enumerator never reads (out of its declared scope, matching Go/Rust's own precedent of not reporting constructors), plus at least one bare-name collision (an interface named 'ChainOptions' exists in two unrelated places in the real source, which name-only fixture matching cannot disambiguate - a pre-existing general risk of the matching convention, not unique to this enumerator).
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: record as a known, honestly-disclosed extraction-fidelity question for pdf/typescript (258 missing, chiefly constructor-parameter-properties; 29 extra, chiefly constructors and one name collision; 1 signature, a rest-parameter naming convention). Not fixed by this card (out of its literal scope - the oracle's job was to build a real, independent diff tool and report what it finds) and not blocking G3. A future card can investigate whether the tree-sitter TypeScript extractor should surface constructor-parameter-properties as members, and whether constructors themselves should be in scope for all languages' oracles, if this pilot is ever re-prioritized for fidelity work.
rationale: Same principle as OQ-018 (cells/rust): the independent oracle's job is to surface real discrepancies honestly, including ones about this project's own extraction fixtures, not only to prove the oracle itself is correct. The two real root causes (constructor-parameter-properties, constructors as a member kind) are structural TypeScript-extraction questions worth a dedicated future investigation, not a quick fix bolted onto the oracle card that found them.

question: TC-592's real live run of the new Java oracle against the real pinned pdf/java commit (aspose-pdf-foss/Aspose.PDF-FOSS-for-Java @ 736cedaa2922e4952f429364bdb9a4bbb1d97863) found a large non-empty diff: missing=499, extra=16301, signature=277, enum_value=542 (checked ~9726). The worker traced every category before reporting, and the causes split into two kinds. (A) Real, structural extraction-fidelity gaps in the baked api_surface.json fixture itself: (1) enum_value=542 - the real tree-sitter Java extractor never captures an enum constant's constructor-argument value at all (every Java enum's baked 'value' field is always an empty string, confirmed by scanning the whole fixture); the independent oracle reads these exactly (e.g. 'AnnotationFlags.Invisible' -> '1 << 0'), so every Java enum with explicit constructor args disagrees. (2) extra~16000 (the dominant category) - the real extractor FLATTENS INHERITED members into each subclass's own served methods/properties list (e.g. Annotation.getMargin/setMargin are served on Annotation but are declared on its base BaseParagraph), which a parse-phase-only oracle correctly cannot and must not replicate without a full class-hierarchy resolver - explicitly out of this card's scope. (3) missing (minor-moderate) - some are genuine real gaps (e.g. Border.getWidth/setWidth/getStyle/setStyle/getDash/setDash declared but not served). (B) Pre-existing, cross-cutting limitations of source_differential.py's own diff engine, exposed more by Java than by Go/Rust/TypeScript/Python: the diff engine matches an oracle symbol to a baked type by BARE NAME alone, with no namespace/package awareness - the pdf/java fixture has 55 distinct class names that occur in 2+ different packages with completely different members (e.g. 'Border' exists in both org.aspose.pdf.annotations and org.aspose.pdf.engine.xfa.model.template), causing oracle symbols to be diffed against the wrong same-named baked type (contributing to missing/signature); separately, Java method overloading (several same-named methods, different parameter lists) is not merged by name-only matching, inflating the signature count, since the diff engine's by-name comparison only meaningfully checks one overload. Neither (B) issue is specific to Java - any language with cross-package name collisions or overloading could hit the same limitation; neither is something a single per-language enumerator card should fix.
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: record both kinds of finding as known, honestly-disclosed gaps. (A) is a pdf/java extraction-fidelity question (inheritance-flattening scope, enum constant values) for a future card if this pilot is ever re-prioritized. (B) is a cross-cutting source_differential.py diff-engine limitation (name-only matching has no namespace scoping and no overload grouping) that a future card should address once at the diff-engine layer, benefiting every language's enumerator at once, rather than patching it per-language. Neither blocks G3; TC-592's own job (build a real, independently-correct Java oracle) is done - it also caught and fixed a real gap in its OWN scope (nested public static types were silently unmatched for ~20% of baked names until the worker found and fixed this mid-investigation, within its own write_paths, which is a success for this card, not a finding against it).
rationale: Same principle as OQ-018 (Rust) and OQ-019 (TypeScript): the independent oracle's job is to surface real discrepancies honestly, including about this project's own extraction fixture AND about the diff-engine's own matching design, not only to prove each new enumerator is itself bug-free. Separating (A) per-pilot extraction questions from (B) a shared diff-engine limitation matters because fixing (B) once (name matching scoped by namespace/package, and grouping overloads before comparison) would improve every already-landed and future enumerator's signal quality at once.

question: TC-593's real live run of the new .NET oracle against the real pinned pdf/net commit (aspose-pdf-foss/Aspose.PDF-FOSS-for-.NET @ b7172877651413cff57a8bfe41fb8a8befb2406b) found: missing=239, extra=6287, signature=292, static=6, enum_value=9. The worker traced every category against the real cloned source. (1) extra~84: C# indexers served as properties by the baked fixture, deliberately out of this oracle's declared scope (documented). (2) extra~490: constructors served as named methods by the baked fixture; every enumerator in this file (Python/Go/Rust/Java/TypeScript) excludes constructors by established convention - not a defect. (3) extra~5700 (dominant): the same inheritance-flattening pattern already found for Java (OQ-020) - confirmed concretely on BleedMarkAnnotation : Annotation (the baked fixture serves 47 properties/8 methods on the subclass that are declared only on the base class); a parse-phase-only oracle correctly cannot replicate this without a semantic/symbol resolver, which is out of scope by design. question: TC-595's fleet run found enumerate_typescript compared ZERO real members for cells/typescript, a silent-looking 'pass' that is actually hollow. Root cause (confirmed by the worker, not merely suspected): cells/typescript's upstream package.json declares "main": "index.ts", but that file is a demo script (console.log/workbook.save calls), not a barrel re-exporting the library's real classes (Cell/Workbook/Chart etc., which clearly exist in the source). enumerate_typescript (TC-591) deliberately scopes to symbols reachable from the package's declared entry point, by design, with no fallback for an entry point that resolves but doesn't actually re-export the library. This is a gap in the oracle's own TypeScript scoping heuristic, not a pdf/typescript-specific issue (TC-591 proved fine on pdf/typescript, which does have a real barrel).
provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: does not block G3. A future card to enumerate_typescript should add a fallback: when the declared entry point resolves but yields zero or near-zero exported classes/interfaces relative to a full-file scan of the package's source tree, fall back to the full-file scan (the same fallback TC-591 already uses when no entry point resolves at all) rather than silently reporting an empty, falsely-passing comparison.
rationale: A zero-member comparison that reads as a clean pass is more dangerous than a loud failure - it hides the fact that no real checking happened at all. Recording this distinctly from OQ-023 since it's an oracle-tooling gap (TypeScript entry-point heuristic), not an extraction-pipeline defect.

question: A partial G3 gate-exit re-verification flagged TC-533 as FLAKY: its two required clean runs disagreed. Investigated directly: run 1 passed cleanly (exit 0, 5116+483 tests, 0 failures). provisional_decision: PROVISIONAL_ACCEPT: does not block G3 by itself - TC-533's own code and negative control are confirmed correct; this is an environment/stability finding, not a defect in the card's own claim. Recommend a future investigation specifically reproduce the access violation (run the exact failing check command standalone, repeatedly, under the same memory/thread pressure a full from-scratch gate-exit run creates) to identify which native dependency is crashing, before deciding whether it needs a code fix, a test-isolation fix (e.g. splitting this card's giant combined check command into smaller ones), or is specific to this host. UPDATE 2026-10-27: re-ran TC-533's full verification (both clean runs plus the negative control) again after the supervisor removed 36 accumulated stale git worktrees (8.37GB) that had built up on this host across the session. It passed cleanly this time: accepted=True, reason 'all gates passed', no access violation. This is consistent with the original crash being a transient resource-pressure artifact of the exceptional circumstances it occurred under (a 14+ hour from-scratch gate-exit run, competing worktree bloat, many concurrent pytest subprocesses), not a reproducible defect in TC-533's own code or test. Restored to ACCEPTED on this evidence - this card is also cited as the closure proof for 9 other audit findings (FK8S-07, ISOPROV-02/03, AGT-01/07, RST-01/04/07/16) and 3 Round-3 rows (RD3-011/012/013), all of which also depend on this status. Notably, this surfaced while re-verifying TC-536 concurrently alongside two other cards (TC-376, TC-567), i.e. under real concurrent load from this session's own newly-added gate-exit parallelization (perf(ops): parallelize gate-exit's per-card re-verification, f4867edf). Strengthens the recommendation: before trusting this host for routine 4-way-parallel gate-exit runs, either (a) identify and fix the crashing native dependency, or (b) as a cheaper mitigation, cap gate-exit's concurrency lower (e.g. 2) specifically for cards whose own check commands are unusually large (thousands of tests in one pytest invocation), or (c) at minimum, always budget for a one-card-at-a-time re-verification pass on any card gate-exit flags as FLAKY before concluding it is broken - two of two 0xC0000005 occurrences so far (TC-533, TC-536) resolved cleanly on an isolated re-run.
